Senses.Note: Four independent works. This body-part sense is distinct from abstract footing or stance.

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云：「死去生來不依本分，過在甚麼處？」師云：「腳跟下好與三十棒。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan (破山禪師語錄). Poshan Haiming is the exact respondent placing a deserved thirty blows beneath the questioner's heel.

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云：「他家自有通霄路。」師云：「腳跟下好與三十棒。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yinyuan (隱元禪師語錄). Yinyuan Longqi is the exact respondent placing a deserved thirty blows beneath the participant's heel.
Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanshan Lai (三山來禪師語錄). Sanshan Lai is the exact speaker saying to put the buddhas beneath the heel.

Occurrences.Kwic: 被者條黑漆索子縛住腳跟，不得自由。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Faxi Yin (法璽印禪師語錄). Faxi Yin is the exact speaker describing a black rope binding the heels and preventing freedom.

Senses.Explanation: The heel, including the physical location beneath it. Poshan Haiming and Yinyuan Longqi place a threatened thirty blows beneath a participant's heel. Sanshan Lai puts the buddhas below the heel, while Faxi Yin describes a black rope binding the heels and preventing free movement. These bodily and spatial predicates retain the ordinary body part even when Chan speakers use its low position for punishment, hierarchy, or constraint.

Senses.Note: Four independent works establish the abstract stance sense through governing verbs of planting, stabilizing, and following.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xueguan (雪關禪師語錄). Xueguan Zhiyin is the exact speaker saying that footing planted on the ground is slippery like moss.

Occurrences.Kwic: 劄向遮裏立得定腳跟麼？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Record of Chan Master Juelang Dasheng of Tianjie (天界覺浪盛禪師全錄). Within his established hall address, Juelang Dasheng is the exact speaker asking whether listeners can stand here with settled footing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 人人鼻孔撩天，箇箇腳跟點地。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tian'an Sheng (天岸昇禪師語錄). Tian'an Sheng is the exact speaker quoting the claim that everyone has nose raised to heaven and heels planted on the ground.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若隨他腳跟轉，落七落八
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baichi (百癡禪師語錄). Baichi Xingyuan is the exact speaker warning that turning after another's heels leaves one falling repeatedly.

Senses.Explanation: One's footing or independent stance rather than the anatomical heel. Xueguan Zhiyin calls the footing planted on the ground slippery as moss. Juelang Dasheng asks whether listeners can stand with settled footing; Tian'an Sheng cites heels planted on the ground as a claim about everyone; Baichi Xingyuan warns that turning after another person's heels leaves one tumbling in dependence. Chan bends the body word into a test of whether someone has a stable and independent place to stand.
